# Button — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for a button when the next step is an action the person intends to take: saving a form, sending a message, opening a dialog. Put one primary action on a screen and give it the filled variant; every lower-emphasis action takes tonal, outlined or text so the hierarchy reads at a glance. A button is not a link — if it moves to another place rather than doing something here, use an anchor, or `LinkButton` when the destination should wear the button treatment. Destructive actions have no variant of their own: `color="danger"` re-paints the five variants in the error roles, which keeps the action vocabulary at five instead of six. A busy button keeps its label and reports it: `loading` swaps in the progress indicator and blocks interaction until it clears. Binary choices get `toggle`: the button morphs round to square when selected, swaps to its emphasis pair, and reports `aria-pressed`.

### Usage

**Do**

- Use filled for important, final actions that complete a flow — Save, Join now, Confirm. It has the most visual impact after the FAB.
- Use tonal where a lower-priority button needs slightly more emphasis than an outline gives — `Next` in an onboarding flow.
- Use outlined for important actions that aren't the main one on the screen.
- Use text for the lowest-priority actions, especially when presenting multiple options.
- Use elevated only when the button needs visual separation from a patterned background — never by default, to prevent shadow creep.
- Use `color="danger"` for destructive actions (delete, discard, remove).
- Use toggle for binary selections like Save or Favorite — outlined icon unselected, filled icon selected.
- Keep toggle labels a similar length in both states so the layout holds.
- Use sentence case, 1–3 words, on a single line that never truncates.
- Place the icon leading (it flips automatically in RTL); use one icon, never two.

**Don't**

- Don't use a button to navigate — if it moves to another place, use an anchor or `LinkButton`.
- Don't stack multiple filled buttons — demote the rest to tonal or outlined.
- Don't put a text label inside `size="icon"` — icon-only means icon plus `aria-label`.
- Don't reach for elevated first — it is a filled tonal with a shadow, reserved for separation cases.
- Don't clutter with too many buttons — move low-priority actions to menus or icon buttons.
- Don't fix the width narrower than the label or stretch to long flat bars.
- Don't vertically stack icon above label or ungroup icon from label.
- Don't use toggle text buttons — there is no selected text treatment.
- Don't underline text buttons — hyperlinked body text carries links.

### FAQ

**When do I use text vs outlined?**

Text for the lowest-emphasis inline actions (dialog secondary actions, inline list actions). Outlined where a visible boundary helps scanning — grouped actions, forms, toolbars.

**How does `loading` differ from `disabled`?**

`loading` shows the progress indicator and reports `aria-busy` while blocking interaction like `disabled`. Use it when the action is in flight; use `disabled` when the action is unavailable.

**Why does `elevated` lift on hover but `filled` doesn't rest elevated?**

Per M3: elevated rests at level1 and lifts to level2 on hover; filled rests at level0 and lifts to level1 on hover. The resting shadow is the variant's identity — only hover adds lift.

## Native

### Features

Reach for a button when tapping causes something: submit, save, open, confirm. The variant axis mirrors the web union exactly — `filled` is the emphasis treatment, `tonal` and `outlined` the quieter pair, `text` the quietest, and `elevated` the one treatment that raises — because the variant law is one meaning per name across both renderers, not one name count. `color="danger"` re-paints any of the five in the error roles instead of adding a sixth vocabulary word. `size` walks the compact `xs`, the default height, the small `sm`, the large `xl` and the square `icon` box. `loading` swaps in the progress indicator and blocks the press until it clears, and `icon` renders beside the label with the same icon `gap` the web pair uses.

### Usage

**Do**

- Put one primary action per screen — the filled button carries the hierarchy.
- Use `color="danger"` for destructive actions instead of inventing a sixth variant.
- Keep labels to a few words — the button resolves its height from the `kern.button.size` scale and truncates long text.
- Use `toggle` for binary Save/Favorite selections with morph and emphasis swap.

**Don't**

- Don't use a button to navigate — navigate with a list item or link, not an action control.
- Don't stack multiple filled buttons — demote the rest to tonal, outlined, or text.
- Don't render a glyph-only button without an accessibility label from the pressable props.
- Don't toggle text — there is no selected text treatment.

| Press feedback | pressed | opacity 0.82 + android_ripple | whole-container dim; ripple follows the treatment ink |
| Container | resting | theme.shape.full | 9999px pill |

### FAQ

**Why does native `elevated` have no shadow?**

On native the raised treatment separates by its `surfaceContainerLow` fill rather than a shadow — the level-1 row is the spec's, not the paint's. The FAB family still carries level-3 shadows.

**How do I get the treatment without the component?**

Use the exported `buttonStyles(variant, size, disabled, theme, options)` — it returns the container and label styles with the same color, shape, and block options.
